narrative: The model estimated a 56% chance that you would be a bad credit risk. In practical terms, this is a slightly stronger signal for default than for repayment, so your application was denied. The decision was driven mainly by your checking account status: it was the single most influential factor and it pushed the prediction toward bad credit. Your account is shown as overdrawn, a situation seen for only about 12.6% of approved applicants, while most approved applicants have no negative balance. The second most influential factor was the amount requested. At 2,600 DM, it is below the approved average of about 3,020 DM, so this factor actually worked in your favor. The third factor, your 18-month loan term, was also slightly shorter than the approved average of about 19.2 months and therefore also pushed toward good credit. Those favorable points were not enough to outweigh the concern created by the overdrawn checking account. To improve your chances, focus first on bringing the checking account into a positive or at least non-negative position and maintaining that for several months. You could also ask the bank what balance history it expects, consider applying with a suitable guarantor or co-applicant, and reapply once your account record is stronger.
